analysis: Changes in ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift: (1) removed the single-ID constant qwen38ConstrainedModelID; advertisesCapability (head line 75) now uses ModelRuntimeRequirements.qwen38ConcreteModelIDs.contains(model.id) plus Qwen35TemplateFix.applies, so the MTP variant (EigenLabs/Qwen3.8-27B-4bit-mtp) can advertise the forced tool-choice capability. (2) validateParser (head line 151) now treats any modelType with prefix "qwen3_5" as nativeQwen, so the framed format .qwen35 or .xmlFunction is accepted instead of .nemotron. Parser acceptance is only reachable after forcedStrategy admits the model, and that still requires Qwen35TemplateFix.applies or nativeStructuredTarget. A non-Qwen model cannot reach the broader prefix match, and Nemotron still rejects .qwen35 (test line 102-107). Tests only add the MTP ID and "qwen3_5" cases. This is tool-call framing and validation rather than a confidentiality or attestation path. It touches no encryption, key, attestation or authorization surface in TB-002/TB-007, and I saw no regression against T-008 or T-041. Not visible in the supplied evidence: ModelRuntimeRequirements.qwen38ConcreteModelIDs contents (the MTP ID's membership and M5/NAX runtime gating), and Qwen35TemplateFix.applies semantics. Test line 101-102 says the legacy Qwen27 ID is filtered without M5/NAX, but the MTP ID's filtering is not asserted in the tests. The next pass should confirm the MTP ID shares the same runtime-capability filter in the registration path (CoordinatorClientCodec) and that withheld post-validation is applied for it.
